senses.gloss: A friendly feeling of togetherness among people who share interests or beliefs.
examples: The church serves coffee after the service to encourage *fellowship*.
There was a warm *fellowship* around the campfire that night.
She missed the *fellowship* of her old running club.

senses.gloss: The ability of a person or animal to produce offspring.
examples: The couple went to a *fertility* clinic after two years of trying.
The country's *fertility* rate has fallen below replacement level.
Stress and smoking can both affect *fertility*.

senses.gloss: A very fine thread of material, such as the plastic thread fed into a 3D printer.
examples: The printer ran out of *filament* halfway through the job.
Under the microscope the mold showed long white *filaments*.
A spider builds its web from *filaments* thinner than a hair.

senses.gloss: A pattern or trace so distinctive that it identifies where something came from.
examples: Every star leaves a chemical *fingerprint* in its light.
The virus has a genetic *fingerprint* that researchers can track.
Analysts matched the software's digital *fingerprint* to an earlier attack.

senses.gloss: A lively, spirited person, often a small one.
examples: Grandma is eighty-two and still a *firecracker*.
Their youngest is a real *firecracker* — she never sits still.
The new point guard is a *firecracker* on defense.

senses.gloss: A wall built to stop a fire from spreading, as between a garage and a house or between a car's engine and its cabin.
examples: Code requires a *firewall* between the garage and the living space.
The wiring runs through a rubber grommet in the *firewall*.
The *firewall* kept the flames out of the second unit.

senses.gloss: A barrier that keeps two parts of an organization separate so one cannot influence the other.
examples: There is supposed to be a *firewall* between the newsroom and the ad department.
The bank keeps a *firewall* between its research and trading desks.
Critics say the *firewall* between the campaign and the outside group is a fiction.

senses.gloss: A dramatic outburst of anger or excitement, used in the plural.
examples: There were *fireworks* at the school board meeting last night.
Expect *fireworks* when those two lawyers are in the same room.
The debate produced more *fireworks* than answers.

senses.gloss: A situation in which everything a person does is open to public view.
senses.ru: жизнь на виду у всех, полная публичность
examples: Living in the governor's mansion means living in a *fishbowl*.
Small-town life can feel like a *fishbowl*.
Fame put the whole family in a *fishbowl*.

senses.gloss: Someone who believes in and supports a leader, a religion, or a set of ideas.
examples: The preacher and his *followers* marched to the courthouse.
The movement's earliest *followers* met in a church basement.
She is a devoted *follower* of the diet's founder.

senses.gloss: The thing or things mentioned next, usually a list.
examples: Please bring the *following*: a photo ID, your lease, and two pay stubs.
Answer the *following* in complete sentences.
The *following* is a summary of the committee's findings.

senses.gloss: A secure position from which further progress can be made.
examples: The company gained a *foothold* in the Asian market last year.
The party is trying to get a *foothold* in the suburbs.
That internship gave her a *foothold* in publishing.

senses.gloss: A small detail or person remembered only as a minor part of a larger story.
examples: The scandal is now just a *footnote* in the city's history.
He worries that one good season will make him a *footnote*.
Their protest became a *footnote* to a much bigger movement.

senses.gloss: The amount of ground or space that a building, machine, or business takes up.
examples: The new store has a much smaller *footprint* than the old one.
They cut the server's *footprint* in half.
The chain expanded its *footprint* into twelve more states.

senses.gloss: The total effect a person or company has on the environment, especially the carbon released.
examples: Flying less is the fastest way to shrink your carbon *footprint*.
The company promised to cut its *footprint* in half by 2030.
Beef has a far bigger *footprint* than beans.

senses.gloss: Competitive public speaking and debate as a school activity.
examples: She joined the *forensics* team her sophomore year.
The *forensics* tournament runs all day Saturday.
He won a state medal in *forensics* for dramatic interpretation.

senses.gloss: The cancellation of a debt, so that it no longer has to be repaid.
examples: The program offers student loan *forgiveness* after ten years of public service.
Some borrowers qualify for partial *forgiveness*.
The bill included *forgiveness* for small-business loans.

senses.gloss: A crack or split in rock or in the earth's crust.
examples: Rainwater works its way into every *fracture* in the limestone.
Geologists mapped the *fractures* along the canyon wall.
Gas escapes through *fractures* deep underground.

senses.gloss: A serious split in a group, a party, or a relationship.
examples: The vote exposed a deep *fracture* within the party.
The strike left a *fracture* between management and the crew.
Old *fractures* in the family reopened at the funeral.

senses.gloss: A set of ideas, rules, or principles used for planning and making decisions.
examples: The two sides agreed on a *framework* for the talks.
Her thesis borrows a *framework* from economics.
The law provides a *framework* for handling complaints.

senses.gloss: A supporting structure of bars, beams, or poles.
examples: The steel *framework* of the tower went up in three weeks.
Vines climbed a wooden *framework* along the fence.
Workers welded the *framework* before adding the panels.

senses.gloss: A series of movies, games, or books built around the same characters or world.
examples: The studio is rebooting the *franchise* with a new cast.
That sequel nearly killed the *franchise*.
The game *franchise* has sold forty million copies.

senses.gloss: A professional sports team that holds a place in a league.
examples: The *franchise* moved to Las Vegas after thirty years downtown.
He's the best player in *franchise* history.
The owners paid a record price for the *franchise*.

senses.gloss: A group of people who share the same profession or interest.
examples: The crash shocked the tight-knit *fraternity* of bush pilots.
She was the first woman admitted to that *fraternity* of surgeons.
Long-haul truckers form a *fraternity* of their own.

senses.gloss: Disagreement or tension between people.
examples: There has been *friction* between the two departments for years.
The new schedule caused some *friction* at home.
A little *friction* on a team is normal.

senses.gloss: An insulting informal word for someone who seems crazy or very strange.
examples: The guy yelling at the parking meter is a total *fruitcake*.
Half the letters we get are from *fruitcakes*.
They treated her like a *fruitcake* for warning them.

senses.gloss: The business of packing and shipping customer orders.
examples: She works nights at a *fulfillment* center outside Columbus.
The company handles its own *fulfillment* instead of hiring a partner.
The delay came from *fulfillment*, not from the factory.

senses.gloss: The purpose something has or the job it is meant to do.
examples: The building's original *function* was a grain store.
Every part of the engine has a clear *function*.
Sleep serves several *functions* in the body.

senses.gloss: A formal or organized social event.
examples: He had to wear a tie to a work *function*.
The hotel hosts weddings and other *functions*.
She skipped the department *function* to finish grading.

senses.gloss: In mathematics, a rule that gives exactly one output for each input.
examples: Graph the *function* and label the intercepts.
Temperature is a *function* of altitude.
The homework covers linear and quadratic *functions*.
